newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen hardliner Raduyev vows "terror" on Russia.
newsitem.headline: Chechen hardliner Raduyev vows "terror" on Russia.

text.p: Salman Raduyev, the hardline rebel fighter who led a bloody hostage raid a year ago, said on Wednesday he did not recognise Chechen elections held on Monday and was planning new terror attacks on Russia.
"At least three Russian cities must be burned to cinders," he told Reuters. "We are working on a major operation codenamed 'Ash'."

Raduyev, who believes that Chechen leader Dzhokhar Dudayev reported killed in a Russian rocket attack last year is still alive, said he would not obey the newly elected Chechen president and would carry out his own war against Russia.

Raduyev's fighters raided the neighbouring ethnic republic of Dagestan in January 1996 and held hundreds of hostages there. Later, rebel leaders blamed the ambitious field commander for ruining the peace process when his men seized 22 Russian policemen in Dagestan last December.

Moderate rebel military commander Aslan Maskhkadov, who according to early returns from Monday's election became the new Chechen president, has vowed to put an end to uncontrolled activities by independent-minded field commanders.
Monday's polls took place after Moscow and rebels struck a peace deal in August under which Russia withdrew the forces it sent in in December 1994 to quell Chechnya's independence bid.
